group: Keys, access and release supply chain
title: Secret embedded in CI output or logging -> Redacted/rejected and security incident raised.
evidence: Every application log line and exception text passes a filter that replaces partner and webhook secrets, bearer tokens, signatures, sealed field values and `password=`-style values with `[redacted]`, and never drops a line or raises (DEV-186, test_log_redaction.py). There is no CI pipeline to scan, a secret of a shape the filter does not know would pass, and no security incident is raised when one is caught.

evidence: Repeating a request with the same key gives one effect (test_orchestration.py, test_partner_events.py). A restart between write and response is not simulated.

title: Queue broker stops for one partner -> Other partner queues continue; affected backlog visible.
evidence: Each webhook delivery is its own row, so one failing address does not stop others (test_webhooks.py). No broker exists and the case is not tested as stated.

title: Patient wrong-recipient event observed -> Containment and CSO escalation; do not deliver/release.
evidence: Nothing models this resilience behaviour yet.

title: Event replay duplicates critical notification -> Idempotency suppresses unsafe duplicate actions.
evidence: The event inbox records each event once per consumer. Not tested against critical notifications here.

title: Region becomes read-only -> Uncertain writes denied, old state explicitly read-only.
evidence: Nothing models this resilience behaviour yet.

title: Partner latency exceeds contract -> Circuit open, local pending state and defined alternate path.
evidence: Each partner connector has a circuit: after 5 failed or timed-out calls in a row it opens, nothing is sent or asked, and operations wait in their own local state; after a cool-down one trial call decides. While a clinic's booking system is paused or stopped, staff may confirm by hand (the alternate path), and the staff app shows it (test_connector_circuit.py, DEV-221). The thresholds are the developer's, not a partner contract's, and slow-but-successful answers are not measured.

title: Restored workflow differs from source evidence -> Reconciliation blocks closure and flags safety event.
evidence: test_orchestration.py: a workflow that disagrees with its history is frozen. No safety event is raised.

title: Unsafe service resumed without CSO clearance -> Feature activation rejected.
evidence: test_readiness.py: a release is not ready without a clinical safety sign-off. Nothing stops an activation.

title: Scheduled backup missing -> Backup coverage alert, recovery objective marked at risk.
evidence: The Google Cloud setup turns on daily Cloud SQL backups with point-in-time recovery and e-mails the on-call address when Cloud SQL logs an error about a backup (DEV-196, DEV-201, `deploy/gcp/`, passes `terraform validate`). A backup that is silently missing (no run at all) is not detected, the log filter still has to be checked against a real instance, and no recovery objective is tracked.

title: Breaking event schema with live old worker -> Compatibility test fails before rollout.
evidence: The events of the last release are frozen in `foundation/released_events.json` (`manage.py freeze_event_contract`). A test, run in CI before anything ships, fails when an event is removed, loses or gains a field, changes a type or stops always carrying a field; a breaking change must be a new `.v2` event. Freezing refuses a catalogue that breaks the last release (test_contracts.py, DEV-212).

title: DB migration breaks prior release -> Rollout stops; documented roll-forward/recovery executed.
evidence: A test fails in CI when any migration drops or renames a column or table, or runs SQL that drops, renames, truncates or deletes, so the release before can still read the database while a rollout runs (test_contracts.py, DEV-212). There is no rollout to stop and no roll-forward runbook has been executed.

title: Release action lacks 2-person authorization -> Gate fails.
evidence: test_readiness.py: no one signs their own release, and no one signs two requirements. Nothing gates a real release.

title: Code rollback would delete required data -> Destructive rollback prohibited; restore compatibility instead.
evidence: Migrations may only add (test above), so rolling the code back never needs a data-losing step, and every data step can be stepped back over (test_contracts.py, DEV-212). Nothing stops a person running a destructive `migrate` backwards by hand.

title: Partner sandbox data accidentally points production -> Connector environment guard blocks operation.

title: Regional on-call fails acknowledgment -> Deputy escalation and traceable incident timeline.
evidence: An incident gets an owner and a deputy (two different support or safety staff); the owner or deputy acknowledges it; a serious one (SEV-0, SEV-1, unknown, or touching safety) nobody acknowledges within 15 minutes is escalated to the deputy once, by timeline entry and a detail-free email to a verified address. Every step is on an append-only timeline (test_incident_oncall.py, DEV-202). No on-call roster or rota, no paging service, and the 15 minutes is the developer's number.
